diagnosis_explanation:
Your stomach and gut had a sudden problem. This is now better.

You also have other health issues. You have bleeding in your gut. Your body also has long lasting swelling in the tissue that holds your bowels. The cause is not known. You also have diabetes. This means your body has trouble using sugar. You have high cholesterol too. Your blood pressure is high. You have swollen veins in your anus. You also have trouble breathing with your lungs. A small spot on your left lung is hardened.
medication_rationale:
Prandin:
This medicine helps control your blood sugar.
It is given because your diabetes is not well controlled.
You may notice your thirst or urination decrease.
Call your doctor if you get a very fast heartbeat.
Also call if you feel very weak or shaky.

Actos:
This medicine helps control your blood sugar.
It is given because your diabetes is not well controlled.
You may notice your thirst or urination decrease.
Call your doctor if you get very swollen feet or ankles.
Also call if you gain weight very quickly.

Lipitor:
This medicine helps lower your cholesterol.
High cholesterol can hurt your heart and blood vessels.
You may notice fewer headaches.
Call your doctor if you get muscle pain or weakness.
Also call if your skin or eyes turn yellow.

Glucophage:
This medicine helps control your blood sugar.
It is given because your diabetes is not well controlled.
You may notice less nausea or an upset stomach.
Call your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing.
Also call if your stomach hurts a lot.

Benicar:
This medicine helps lower your blood pressure.
High blood pressure can harm your heart and blood vessels.
You may feel less dizzy.
Call your doctor if your face or lips swell.
Also call if you feel very lightheaded.

Advair:
This medicine helps you breathe more easily.
It opens up your airways in the lungs.
You may feel less short of breath.
Call your doctor if your breathing gets worse.
Also call if you get a rash or hives.

Prednisone 15 mg:
This medicine is a steroid that reduces swelling.
It is given to help with inflammation.
You may feel more energetic.
You might get hungry more often.
Call your doctor if you have mood changes.
Also call if your blood sugar gets too high.

recovery_trajectory:
**Week 1:**
- You will likely feel weak and tired this week.
- Focus on drinking clear liquids.
- Eat only clear liquids for now.
- This includes water, broth, and clear juices.
- Call your doctor if you have severe stomach pain.
- Call your doctor if you cannot keep liquids down.
- Your goal this week is to stay hydrated with clear liquids.

**Week 2:**
- You may start to feel a little more energy.
- Slowly add soft, bland foods to your diet.
- Examples include toast, crackers, and rice.
- Avoid dairy, fatty foods, and spicy foods.
- Call your doctor if your stomach pain gets worse.
- Call your doctor if you see blood in your stool.
- Your goal this week is to eat small amounts of bland food.

**Week 3:**
- Your energy levels should continue to improve.
- You can gradually add more foods back.
- Continue to avoid very fatty or spicy foods.
- You can start light walking around your home.
- Call your doctor if you have ongoing vomiting.
- Call your doctor if you have frequent watery stools.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 5 minutes twice a day.

**Week 4:**
- You should feel much stronger this week.
- You can likely return to most normal foods.
- Listen to your body and eat what feels good.
- Continue to avoid heavy or greasy meals for now.
- Call your doctor if your stomach still feels very upset.
- Your goal this week is to walk for 10 minutes daily.

**When to expect improvement:**
- Most people feel much better after a few weeks.
- Keep your diet light if your stomach is sensitive.
- You can increase your activity as you feel stronger.
- Your recovery should continue to progress steadily.
escalation_guide:
CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
These symptoms are life-threatening. Do not drive yourself.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

GO TO THE ER TODAY
Do not wait until tomorrow. Go within a few hours.
- No symptoms in this tier for your diagnosis.

CALL YOUR DOCTOR
Call during office hours. Do not go to the ER for these.
- Questions about your medicine: Your doctor can explain doses.
- Trouble breathing when active: Your COPD may be worse.
- Blood sugar too high: This could make you feel sick.
- Blood sugar too low: This could make you feel dizzy.
- Mild belly pain continues: This could be inflammation returning.
- Nausea but no vomiting: You might feel better soon.
- Wounds healing slowly: Check for signs of infection.
- Hemorrhoid pain continues: You may need creams or other care.
- Feeling tired: This can happen when you recover.
